original_question: Find the exact value of Dno3l(n), the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set with no three collinear points.
target_in_paper: Section 3's exact-value problem for planar sets with no collinear triples: determine D_no3(n) (called Dno3(n) in the 2014 PDF draft; this appears as Problem 6 in the current arXiv version and as Problem 8 in the June 7, 2014 PDF draft).
correct_elements: Your draft already matches the paper's intended problem very closely: it asks for the exact value, concerns the minimum number of distinct distances, works in the plane, and imposes the no-three-collinear restriction. This is precisely the restricted planar distinct-distances problem singled out in Section 3.
missing_details: The paper's notation is Dno3(n), i.e. D_{no3}(n), not Dno3l(n).
The ambient space should be stated explicitly as the Euclidean plane R^2.
To be fully stand-alone, one should define D(P) as the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of distinct points of P.
The minimization should be written explicitly: over all sets P subseteq R^2 with |P| = n and no three points of P collinear.
It should be clear that 'exact value' means the value for each integer n (not merely an asymptotic order of growth).
For paper-faithful context, the nearby discussion records the bounds ceil((n-1)/3) <= Dno3(n) <= floor(n/2), and notes Szemeredi's conjecture that Dno3(n) = floor(n/2).
refined_question: For each positive integer n, let D(P) denote the number of distinct Euclidean distances determined by pairs of distinct points of a finite set P subseteq R^2, and define D_no3(n) = min{D(P) : P subseteq R^2, |P| = n, and no three points of P are collinear}. Determine the exact value of D_no3(n) for every n.
justification: The draft is targeting the paper's exact-value restricted-planar problem for sets with no three collinear points. In the introduction the paper defines D(P) and the unrestricted quantity D(n). In Section 3 it then introduces Dno3(n) exactly as the minimum number of distinct distances determined by an n-point planar set with no collinear triple, gives the regular n-gon upper bound floor(n/2), records Szemeredi's lower bound ceil((n-1)/3), and states the official open problem 'Find the exact value of Dno3(n).' The only substantive issue in the draft is the notation typo Dno3l(n) instead of Dno3(n), together with a few implicit definitions that should be made explicit to make the question fully self-contained. Note also that the numbering differs by version: the same question is Problem 8 in the June 7, 2014 PDF draft and Problem 6 in the current arXiv version, but the mathematical content is the same.
